html: Two papers accepted to WACV! GeoDIVE (Geospatial Descent Informed by Value Estimation) and GenOpticalFlow, a generative approach to unsupervised optical flow learning. Congrats to Hamza Iqbal, Daniel Cher, Eric Xing, Feng Qiao, and Zhexiao Xiong.
ActWorld was accepted to NeurIPS! It turns explorable world models into interactive ones with action-aware memory. Congrats to first author Zhexiao Xiong.

🏆 TerraDiT won the Best Paper Award at the ECCV TerraBytes workshop! It generates satellite imagery conditioned on a handful of points on a map. Huge congrats to Srikumar Sastry, Daniel Cher, Brian Wei, Aayush Dhakal, Subash Khanal, and Dev Gupta. What a way to wrap up Malmö!

Genesis was accepted to ACM SIGSPATIAL! It's a generative engine for hierarchical satellite image synthesis. Congrats to Subash Khanal, Ice Cui, Daniel Cher, Eric Xing, Brian Wei, and Srikumar Sastry.

Four papers headed to ECCV in Malmö! 🇸🇪 TrajLoc geo-localizes a moving camera from a sequence of observations, TerraDiT-Ω controls satellite image synthesis with any geospatial primitive, and UniDrive-WM is a driving world model that unifies understanding, planning, and generation. And Tessellating the Earth learns a location encoder that tiles the globe into movable Voronoi cells, putting more detail where the world is more varied. Congrats to Brian Wei, Tianyi Gao, Daniel Cher, Zhexiao Xiong, Srikumar Sastry, Jonathan Lin, Danni Beaulieu, Hamza Iqbal, and Eric Xing.

Three papers accepted to CVPR. See you in Denver! 🏔️ ProM3E is a probabilistic multimodal embedding model for ecology, SimLBR learns to detect fake images by learning what real ones look like, and PRUE is a practical recipe for segmenting field boundaries at scale. Congrats to Aayush Dhakal, Subash Khanal, Srikumar Sastry, Jonathan Lin, Daniel Cher, and Phoenix Jarosz.
🌱 Zhexiao Xiong is heading to ByteDance for a spring internship. Have fun!
DiffVAS was accepted to AAMAS! It uses diffusion models to guide visual active search when only part of the environment can be seen. Congrats to Srikumar Sastry.
🎓 Srikumar Sastry successfully defended his PhD proposal. One big step closer!

VectorSynth made it into WACV in the second round! It synthesizes satellite images from structured semantic maps, with fine-grained control over what goes where. Congrats to Daniel Cher, Brian Wei, and Srikumar Sastry. See you in Tucson! 🌵
